text:
maria: Heads-up — we hit a weird routing tie in staging when a host wildcard and a path regex both have capture groups. Two services got matched intermittently for the same request. Repro below.

maria: Example rules (simplified):
```
- host: "*.example.com" -> svc: default-svc
- host: "api.{region}.example.com" -> svc: regional-svc
- path: "/files/(.+)" -> svc: file-service
- path: "/files/(?<id>\d+)" -> svc: file-id-service
```

maria: Request: host=api.us-east.example.com path=/files/123
Expected: regional-svc + file-id-service => routed to file-id-service on regional cluster.
Observed: sometimes default-svc + file-service is picked.

ken: Hmm. Do we have any nondeterministic sort in the matcher? We should have a deterministic precedence algorithm: exact host > host with capture > host wildcard, and for path: exact literal > regex with named capture > regex generic > wildcard.

oliver: We do score routes, but the scoring mixes host and path weights and then sorts by insertion order for ties. In this case the host wildcard score equals the more-specific host because of a bug in host-segment scoring for capture tokens. That explains the flip when we reload rules.

sam: Unfortunate. Two quick asks: (1) can we change tie-breaker to prefer longer matched literal length instead of insertion order? (2) add a debug header that surfaces the matching score/decision chain for a request so ops can troubleshoot? :mag:

maria: +1 on debug header. For (1) I'm wary of length-only: "api.{region}.example.com" vs "*.example.com" both match but the literal parts differ nontrivially. Maybe compute specificity vector: (host_literal_chars, host_capture_count (less better), path_literal_chars, path_regex_specificity). Sort by vector lexicographically.

ken: I like specificity vector. Also we should treat named vs unnamed captures differently: named captures are usually intentionally tighter. So treat named-capture as slightly higher specificity than unnamed.

oliver: Note on perf: moving to a heavier comparator for every request could add CPU. We already precompute route scores at config load; tie-breaker should be deterministic using precomputed keys — we can compute the specificity vector once per route and then compare vector tuples cheaply at request time.

maria: Good point. Implementation plan: patch score calc to produce tuple: [host_literal_chars, -host_named_captures, -host_total_captures, path_literal_chars, path_regex_named_groups, path_regex_total_groups, insertion_seq_rev] so higher tuple sorts earlier. Keep insertion_seq_rev as last fallback.

sam: For UX: when a rule is overridden by header-based override (X-Route-Override), we should log an event and include a short note in the debug header. Ops keep tripping on silent header overrides during smoke tests.

ken: Agree. Also we should add a unit test matrix that covers combos: host wildcards + host captures, path regex named vs unnamed, header overrides, and confirm deterministic selection with reloads.

routing-bot: Automated check queued: route-matcher-spec-change. CI will run matcher unit matrix and a small perf harness. ETA 2 days.

maria: I'll open the RFC doc and include the specificity vector definition, sample scoring table, and example conflict resolution. Putting a few real production rule snapshots in the RFC will help.

oliver: Quick note — watch out for backcompat: existing customers might rely on insertion order. We should add a migration flag to opt-in the new deterministic ordering before flipping globally.

maria: Yep — feature flag + migration window. I'll draft the RFC and a short changelog blurb for the console (so customers understand why a different route now wins).

sam: Thanks all. If routing-bot reports green, can we roll a canary tomorrow morning? :thumbsup:

routing-bot: CI started. Will post results in this thread when complete.
